newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore telecom firms networks with US and Can.
newsitem.headline: Singapore telecom firms networks with US and Can.

text.p: Singapore said on Tuesday it will organise events during a major telecommunications conference to encourage joint ventures of local telecom companies with firms in the United States and Canada.

"We want to raise local profiles in other countries and encourage joint ventures between the private sector in our country and US and Canada," said spokeswoman Valerie D'Costa of the Telecomunications Authority of Singapore (TAS).
"Brokerage events with U.S. and Canada fit in with TAS's role to provide Singapore's national telecom industry with international networking," she told a news conference.
So-called brokerage events -- staged to bring several parties together -- will be part of the Asia Telecom 97 exhibition to be held in Singapore from June 9 to 14.
There is high-level support from American and Canadian telecom companies for the brokerage events, D'Costa said.

"Americans are the leaders in telecommunications technologies," D'Costa told Reuters. "We are trying to position Singapore companies to be able to add value to the American experience in Singapore," she added.

Canada's smaller telecom companies appealed to TAS, D'Costa said. "Through our government to government contact we have found there are very good smaller companies in Canada hoping to attract the Asian market."
Asia Telecom '97 is a exhibition and forum to be attended by over 450 companies from more than 30 countries showcasing their latest products and services.
